I fetched the Internet Archive scan text directly (item appealtochrist00grimke) and read the passage in the OCR: the objection runs “But perhaps you will be ready to query, why appeal to women on this subject? We do not make the laws which perpetuate slavery. No legislative power is vested in us; we can do nothing to overthrow the system, even if we wished to do so. To this I reply, I know you do not make the laws, but I also know that you are the wives and mothers, the sisters and daughters of those who do; and if you really suppose you can do nothing to overthrow slavery, you are greatly mistaken. You can do much in every way; four things I will name. 1st. You can read on this...” Every word of the shipped line is there in order, the cut at “To this I reply,” is honest and the note declares it, and the sentence genuinely ends at “mistaken.” The page marker 16 stands before the passage and 17 after it, so p. 16 is right, and “answering why appeal to women” is exactly what the paragraph does, immediately before the four things she will name. Not a translation, so no drift to check. Not scripture, film, lyric, proverb, business or oratory: it is a written pamphlet, so the Essay tag is the form of the work. 1836, well before 1999. shipped.js: not shipped, no near match, angelina grimke 0 of 3, not banned. First, the evidence field names the edition as “revised and corrected”; the scan the evidence itself cites is not that printing, it is The Anti-Slavery Examiner, Vol. I, September 1836, No. 2, signed A. E. Grimke, and it carries no revision notice. The shipped source line says only “American Anti-Slavery Society, 1836”, which is correct for the Examiner printing, so the line ships clean and only the evidence note overreaches. Second, the byline. The card prints the author name alone, and “Angelina Grimké” is shared with Angelina Weld Grimké, her great-niece, the Harlem Renaissance poet, whom a reader is as likely to picture at six in the morning. The year already carries her sister as “sarah moore grimke”, so the fuller form is the house habit.
